I am recommending against high-yield BB-rated bonds due to their lower credit ratings and greater default risks compared to investment-grade bonds. To implement a laddered maturity structure, I would recommend allocating 0.30 to 5-year BBB+ bonds and 0.20 to 10-year BBB+ bonds. This would ensure minimal exposure to high-yield debt and spread maturing bonds across 5 and 10-year buckets. A laddered maturity structure helps maintain portfolio stability as it avoids over-concentration in short- or long-term bonds.

The recommended laddered maturity structure is:
- 30% of the portfolio allocated to bonds maturing in 5 years
- 20% of the portfolio allocated to bonds maturing in 10 years

This structure meets the constraint of no more than 30% maturing in any single year and maintains a portfolio duration below 10 years, adhering to both the investment-grade requirement and the specified max_duration_years constraint. This is within the specified credit rating limits, with BBB+ being the lowest rating considered due to the min_credit_rating constraint.
